messages:
maria: Heads-up — I sketched a flow for handling weird GPU signal combos (ECC spikes + Xid bursts + PCIe errors) that reduces unnecessary hard-evicts. Wanted quick feedback before I turn it into a runbook.

alex: love the idea of a probation step. TL;DR?

maria: Probation -> Quarantine -> Replace. Probation = soft-cordon with live telemetry probation window (30m) and migration-first policy. Quarantine = hard-cordon + job eviction if signals persist. Replace = mark for hardware swap and reimage.

raj: how does this work for hybrid clusters (k8s + slurm)? we can't just drain everything the same way.

maria: Good call. Proposal: cluster-aware handlers. For k8s: add taint redwood.com/gpu-probation=true:PreferNoSchedule + annotate node with reason and thresholds. For Slurm: set node state to DRAIN with reason and a time-window tag so the scheduler migrates eligible jobs but doesn't preempt reserved/committed jobs.

olivia: can you paste the proto-config?

maria: sure — here's the prototype policy blob we tested locally:

```yaml
policy_name: gpu_probation_quarantine_v1
signals:
  - name: ecc_spike_rate
    threshold: 2/minute
    window: 5m
    consecutive: 3
  - name: xid_error_rate
    threshold: 10/hour
    window: 1h
    consecutive: 2
  - name: pcie_errors
    threshold: 5/10m
    window: 10m
    consecutive: 2
debounce: 300s # wait before acting on transient blips
probation_duration: 1800s # 30m
actions:
  probation: 
    k8s: add_taint: redwood.com/gpu-probation=true:PreferNoSchedule
    slurm: scontrol update NodeName=%NODE% State=DRAIN Reason=GPU_PROBATION_{{id}}
  quarantine:
    k8s: taint: redwood.com/gpu-quarantine=true:NoSchedule; cordon=true
    slurm: scontrol update NodeName=%NODE% State=DRAIN
```

samira: debouncing looks sane. What about jobs that cannot be migrated (checkpointless training)? We should avoid killing those in Dedicated / committed pools.

maria: Agreed — policy has an exclusions list: dedicated_pools and jobs with label "no_migration" get alerted but not auto-evicted; we send an Ops paging and put node into soft-probation so traffic routing can avoid it.

alex: how do we detect recovery? sometimes a kernel reset clears Xid counts and card works fine.

maria: recovery path: if during probation the signals fall below thresholds for two consecutive windows, remove probation taint and add annotation gpu.probation.recovered=true timestamp=... If a node recovers once, we keep it instrumented with elevated sampling for 24h. If it flaps (probation->quarantine->recover) twice in 7d -> auto-schedule hardware replacement.

raj: Slurm side: when you do scontrol update NodeName=x State=DRAIN, are we setting Reason and a TTL to auto-clear if node recovers? Otherwise we have ops chasing stale drain states.

maria: yes — scontrol uses Reason=GPU_PROBATION_ID and we also push a metadata tag to the node record with expiry = now + probation_duration. A periodic reconciler clears state if expiry passed and no active signals.

kube-bot: [info] Applying taint redwood.com/gpu-probation=true to node gpu-node-42 (probation_id=abc123).

oncall-bot: [pager] Node gpu-node-42 entered quarantine window (probation expired) — taking no-evict quarantine action in eu-west1; alerting infra-oncall.

olivia: Region-awareness is key. We shouldn't migrate heavy training off a EU region during a regional maintenance window where spare capacity = 0. Policy should consult region capacity API and only escalate to quarantine if region spare_capacity_pct > 5% or dedicated-reserved impact is acceptable.

maria: yep included: pre-checks: (1) reserved_capacity_impact < 10% OR (2) region_spare > min_spare_threshold -> proceed. Otherwise, mark node for manual ops with message.

samira: cost angle — migrating big jobs to on-demand elsewhere may blow OOB budgets. Do we annotate cost_estimate in the auto-escalation message?

maria: Added: before any cross-region migration we estimate projected extra-GPU-hours and attach to the Ops ticket and to the node annotation. Auto-migration turned off if projected cost delta > configured threshold for the team or pool.

alex: testing plan?

maria: rollout plan: 1) simulate signals in staging; 2) enable probation-only (no auto-quarantine) for 2 weeks in canary fleet; 3) enable full flow in one region during low-traffic window; 4) 30-day observation then global. I'll open the PR for reconciler + policy table.

raj: +1. Also add a metric for false-positive rate (probation -> recovery within window) and track per-hardware-model so we can tune thresholds per-GPU SKU.

maria: done — metrics: gpu.probation.count, gpu.quarantine.count, gpu.recoveries.count, gpu.replacements.scheduled. We'll tag by node_label gpu.sku.

olivia: can we also surface a small explainer in Console node view showing last 24h signal timeline and probation reason? Ops loves context.

maria: yep — UI team asked for the annotation feed. I'll propose a minimal timeline widget.

samira: thanks — this would cut down on noisy hard-evicts. Happy to review the PR.

maria: thanks all — I'll paste the runbook draft into #eng-infra-runbooks once PR merges.
